subject: evs
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Describe themselves in speech and in simple writing: likes, dislikes and hobbies, and respect other people's
Say what the external body parts and sense organs do
Draw a self-portrait and label the external body parts
Solve shadow puzzles and find body parts in a picture
Look after their body parts and sense organs
Notice how people differ, and appreciate those differences
Make their own name card with a logo
Name their own feelings and other people's, and manage them
Name extended family members and say how each is related to them
Draw a family tree that includes distant relatives
Describe how festivals and national days are celebrated at home, at school and in the neighbourhood
Understand why loud crackers, loud music and chemical colours should be avoided
Look after pets with empathy and compassion
Show care and concern for old, sick and differently abled people
Appreciate the help neighbours give one another
Describe the role of each family member, and their own role
Name common food items, such as cereals, pulses, fruits, vegetables and milk
Say why the body needs food
Sort food by where it comes from: plants or animals
Know that different foods help the body in different ways: energy, body building, repair, protection and water
Tell healthy food from junk food, and say why junk food is not good
Respect the variety of food eaten by different families and peers
Care for food and avoid wasting it
Name natural and man-made sources of water, such as rain, lake, river, well and hand pump
Say how plants, animals and people need water
Know some ways to purify drinking water at home and school
Know, at an awareness level, what causes water pollution
Notice that many foods contain water
Suggest ways to stop misusing water and to re-use it
Take sensible precautions in the rain, such as using an umbrella and raincoat
Make slogans and drawings about saving water
Name the different types of houses in cities, villages and other parts of the world
Give reasons why houses are different from one another
Name the materials used to build different houses
Draw and label the parts of a house
Explain why light and fresh air matter in a house
Keep the house and household things clean
Make a simple model of a house and decorate it
Explain why living things need clothes
Name materials used for clothes, such as cotton, silk, wool, canvas and rayon
Tell natural fibres from man-made fibres, with examples
Say which clothes suit which season: cotton in summer, silk and wool in winter, rayon and synthetic in the rains
Draw and label clothes worn by boys and girls
Suggest ways to care for cotton and silk clothes at home
Make clothes-related origami, such as paper dresses
Show, with help from elders, that air has weight, takes up space and expands
Observe and describe some properties of air
Name the causes of air pollution, including smoke and fumes
Suggest ways to deal with smoke and fumes that pollute the air
Name some diseases that spread through the air, and how to prevent them
Do simple breathing exercises, asanas and deep breathing for healthy living
Write slogans and songs to prevent air pollution

topics.topic: Keeping Oneself Clean, Safe and Healthy
covers: Find reasons for filth and garbage around them
Use dustbins and separate wet and dry garbage
Describe how garbage is thrown away at home and in the neighbourhood
Know the benefits of exercise, yoga and games
Take part in play, recreation and outdoor games
Recognise good touch and bad touch, and talk about them with trusted adults
Keep themselves safe from household tools
Explain the proverb that cleanliness is next to godliness
Draw a map of the places in their locality
Explain why public places are needed in a neighbourhood
Name each place and say what it is used for
Name people who help us, such as the postman, a courier worker, a gas delivery worker and a mason
Know where to get help in an emergency: the police station and the fire brigade
Name recreation places in the neighbourhood
Act out community helpers and say how each one helps
Revisit what they learnt about plants in Class I
Name the parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed) and say what each one does
Tell plants that grow on land, in water and as climbers apart, with examples
Name plant products used in daily life
Understand how some plant parts change shape to suit their use, such as underground stems and roots
Name medicinal plants such as tulsi, neem, clove and ginger
Appreciate tree planting and look after plants
Revisit what they learnt about animals in Class I
Name the body parts of pet animals
Describe what animals do: they move, grow and eat
Name the homes of animals: underground, in trees, near water and under water
Understand why animals need shelter
Explain the life cycle of a butterfly
Sort animals by their habits, features and food
Show care and compassion for pets and other animals
Name the transport seen in the neighbourhood and in cities
Name the fuels that run vehicles: petrol, diesel, CNG and electricity
Compare the traffic in cities and in villages
Give reasons for traffic jams, and suggest ways to reduce them
Discuss how vehicles cause air and noise pollution
Value wheelchairs and ramps in schools and public places
Suggest ways to save petrol and diesel
Draw or stick pictures of different vehicles
Explain why communication matters in daily life
Name the ways people communicate in cities and public places
Discuss the good and bad uses of different ways of communicating
Know, at an awareness level, how email, SMS and the internet are used
Use communication for fun and recreation
Know how to guard against misuse of phones and other devices
Demonstrate some ways of communicating

topics.topic: The World Around Me: Sun, Moon, Sky and Stars
covers: Name the heavenly bodies seen in the day and at night
Tell the sun, moon and stars apart by what they look like
Describe the sky in the day, in the afternoon and at night
Draw the heavenly bodies, and sunny, cloudy and rainy days
Know, through pictures, what the solar system is and how day and night happen
Read simple symbolic maps and route maps
Write or collect poems, songs and pictures about the sky
Tell the parts of a day apart: morning, afternoon, evening and night
Talk about what they did today and yesterday, and what they will do tomorrow
Know left and right, above and below, near and far, and up and down
Give and follow simple directions
Describe where objects are: on, in, below or above
Find places and objects in their surroundings, with help identifying directions
Make a scrapbook or picture map of their day and their surroundings
